items.claim: This unit's own onset at Jer.31.35 is warranted only by a bare koh-amar recurrence, the same kind of signal this unit's own rejected alternative treats as insufficient to justify a second cut at Jer.31.37.
items.evidence: The span opens by citing a fresh koh-amar at Jer.31.35 as its whole warrant, naming no addressee shift, scene shift, discourse imperative, date onset, or vision opening, and stating no change in who is speaking from the material immediately before it: Jer.31.31-34 is itself an unbroken oracle to the same audience, closing on a forgiveness formula with no participant change carried into Jer.31.35. This unit's own rejected alternative then declines a further cut at Jer.31.37's own koh-amar because it repeats the same if-then structure already used "with the same speaker and the same audience" as Jer.31.35-36 — that is, because no change in who is speaking accompanies it. That identical test is never run against the span's own opening seam: nothing states what changes in speaker, audience, or discourse mode between Jer.31.34 and Jer.31.35. Both onsets share the same speaker and the same implied audience; the only named difference is topic, which the span's own logic elsewhere treats as insufficient by itself to mark a fresh unit.

items.claim: This unit's own close at Jer.31.40 never states a warrant for stopping there, leaving that shared boundary disclosed only from the far side.
items.evidence: The span narrates its content through the end of Jer.31.40 and stops, but nothing in the row states why the range does not continue into Jer.32.1 — no mention of the dated word-event header that opens there, no discussion of any change in speaker, addressee, or scene at that seam. This unit's own front seam is fully warranted by contrast: the fresh incipit at Jer.31.38 is explicitly named as a fresh topic against the cosmic-oath material just closed. No equivalent statement covers the back seam, even though it is warranted by heavier material (a dated word-event header) than the front seam carries.

items.claim: The onset at Jer.32.1 is carried by both of its own tier-1 signals, and the three layers of embedded speech inside the span are correctly kept from being read as an independent onset.
items.evidence: The header at Jer.32.1 is read as both a word-event formula and a date header, named on their own separate terms rather than folded into one undifferentiated label. Inside the span, an oracle formula appears at Jer.32.3, but it is correctly read as an earlier oracle quoted inside a king's own question, itself reported by the narrator, rather than counted as an independent onset. The close at Jer.32.5/32.6 is carried by a real grammatical change: verses 2-3 describe Jeremiah and Zedekiah in the third person (“Jeremiah the prophet was shut up” web:Jer.32.2; “Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up” web:Jer.32.3), while verse 6 turns to Jeremiah's own first-person voice (“Jeremiah said,” web:Jer.32.6, “Yahweh’s word came to me” web:Jer.32.6) — a concrete, checkable shift rather than an asserted one.

items.claim: The command, performance, and interpretation phases of the field-purchase sign are correctly held as one unit through the deed-signing detail, and the mid-verse formatting break at Jer.32.8 is correctly excluded as evidence.
items.evidence: Nothing between the command (Jer.32.6-8) and the interpretation charge (Jer.32.14-15) changes speaker or addressee: the purchase, weighing, sealing, witnessing, and delivery all continue one first-person report, and the koh-amar at Jer.32.14 is correctly read as a repetition of an oracle already given rather than as an independent onset. A paragraph break inside Jer.32.8 is identified as a modern formatting artifact and explicitly excluded from the boundary argument. The close at Jer.32.15/32.16 is carried by a real mode change, from reporting the purchase to addressing God directly.

items.claim: Both edges of the prayer are carried by real mode changes, and the hymn-like praise inside it is reasoned through on the shape of its own close rather than mistyped by the form of its middle alone.
items.evidence: The unit opens on a prayer-address verb turning the narration from report to direct address, and closes where a fresh word-event formula reopens address as a reply from the other party — a formally marked seam on both counts. The extended praise and historical recital in the middle (Jer.32.17-23) is genuinely hymn-like in form, and this is weighed directly rather than ignored; the unit is still held together as one because it does not close on praise but on an unresolved question (“Is there anything too hard for me?” web:Jer.32.27 answers “There is nothing too hard for you” web:Jer.32.17 just past this unit's own end), matching the shape its own close takes rather than the shape of its middle.

items.claim: The internal cut at Jer.32.36 splits a single, unchanged-speaker reply that opens at the word-event onset in Jer.32.26, and a verse quoted in Hebrew inside the span carries a known textual variant with no disclosure beside that quotation.
items.evidence: This unit's own rejected alternative states plainly that holding the whole reply from Jer.32.26 through the chapter's end as one unit was considered, and that no change in who is speaking interrupts that stretch anywhere; it nonetheless cuts at Jer.32.36 on a compound turn-phrase and a reintroduced quoted-objection construction, neither of which is a change in who is speaking, an addressee shift to a new party, a discourse imperative, a date onset, or a vision opening. A further cut is declined one seam later, at Jer.32.42/32.43, on the identical ground that neither carries a change in who is speaking — which only sharpens the inconsistency of cutting at Jer.32.36 on weaker grounds than that. Separately, the Hebrew of Jer.32.35 is quoted directly in the boundary reasoning without noting there that the verse carries a ketiv/qere variant; that variant is disclosed only later, elsewhere in the row, not beside the quotation itself.

items.claim: The span is held together by the same unchanged-speaker test applied rigorously to its own later material, and its recurring-language observations carry a named, counted sweep rather than a bare uniqueness assertion.
items.evidence: Further cuts are declined at Jer.32.42 and Jer.32.43, where fresh formulas recur, on the express ground that neither carries a change in who is speaking or in addressee, applying that test consistently within the span's own material. The close at Jer.32.44/33.1 is carried by a fresh word-event formula rather than by the chapter division alone. The two recurring-phrase observations (the quoted-objection construction and the captivity-reversal formula) each carry a counted sweep naming the object and the verses involved rather than an unsupported "nowhere else" assertion.

items.claim: The onset at Jer.33.1 is a genuine, independently attested word-event verse rather than an assumed one, its scene continuity with the prior imprisonment setting is disclosed across the chapter division, and the internal formula it declines to cut on is tied to real grammatical subordination rather than a bare topic label.
items.evidence: Jer.33.1's word-event formula belongs to the small set of verses independently identified as carrying that exact formula, so the onset here is not an assumed one. The unit also names that its opening setting, still shut up in the court of the guard, matches the setting of the material immediately before the chapter division, correctly treating that division as no seam by itself. Inside the span, a further koh-amar at Jer.33.4 is declined as a cut point because it opens with a causal particle binding it back to the invitation just made at Jer.33.3, a syntactic dependency rather than a merely asserted continuity.
